items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I worked there with Max Kaminsky

ctx.x: Yeah, because also the music had a sense of fun to it. And I like those clubs where people were drinking and talking and romancing and flirting and were quarreling and fighting, and the music’s going on and everything is all, it’s all part of life. And I think that’s why the jazz sounded that way, it had so much color and flare and fervor and if you like, drunken whatever. I love those places, those sleazy bars. It’s wonderful. You get just a piano player. People would tell me Willie “The Lion” Smith would be…
Well I’m glad that there seems to be at least a small and loyal market for the kind of music that you’re fond of. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
